items.reason: The Planning decision-table test proves the extracted closeout claim boundary, while the ownership contract test proves the review-scale metric ratchet; these are distinct narrow trust questions already owned by retained suites.

Verification package tests are the narrow owner for deterministic exact-subject admission and typed rejection semantics; source-checkout reports exercise the existing integration surface without adding a duplicate root test.

The existing compact-runner contract test is the narrow executable owner for liveness output, rate limiting, result metadata, and short-command silence; a fake clock/process keeps the evidence deterministic without expanding the broader CLI suite.

The change adds focused CLI contract coverage for the startup guardrail and implement tiny-output routing; the evidence belongs with package-local runtime behavior rather than a broad regression matrix.
